title: Same-lineage track restoration: does iTunes accept a library whose only track itlkit deleted and then restored from a donor snapshot?
evidence_class_if_completed: A (observed now, with call metadata and captured artefacts)
question: iTunes has accepted itlkit-written libraries that changed playlist structure (EXP-03, EXP-04) and one that changed a track's text fields (EXP-05B). Every one of those preserved each track's local numeric record ID. EXP-06 is the first experiment in which a track's local ID changes: trackops.add_track_from allocates a fresh local ID for the restored record and fresh persistent IDs for its playlist memberships. The question is whether iTunes accepts that, or whether it cross-checks local IDs against state it keeps outside the .itl file.

construction.step_1: read the donor library with itlkit; the donor is the library iTunes itself wrote when it quit at the end of the EXP-05B restart-2 session
construction.step_2: trackops.delete_track(reduced, PID) on a copy, producing a library with zero tracks
construction.step_3: trackops.add_track_from(reduced, donor, PID), restoring the track from the donor snapshot
construction.nothing_else_is_touched: the media file, the artwork, the sidecar databases (Extras, Genius) and the preferences plist are left exactly as iTunes left them

gate_relaxation.why: trackops.delete_track and trackops.add_track_from both call trackops._profile, which calls operations.require_simple_library, which calls Library._require_semantic_profile. That refuses the live 12.13.11.1 build, which is not in the accepted profile set.
gate_relaxation.mechanism: research/g4/exp03/gate_bypass.py operation_version_spoofed(), the same wider relaxation EXP-05B used
gate_relaxation.licensing_consequence: EXP-06 therefore licenses no wider a claim than EXP-05B about which iTunes builds itlkit may write for. It is evidence about the writer's structural correctness, not about the version gate being too strict.

reasons_for: three prior native experiments show iTunes accepts containers this writer produces
the restored record is a byte-copy of a node iTunes itself wrote, with only ID fields rewritten
assert_pool_bindings and the master-playlist check run before the file is written
reasons_against: this is the first candidate in which a track's local record ID changes
playlist membership persistent IDs are freshly allocated rather than reused
iTunes Library Extras.itdb and iTunes Library Genius.itdb are keyed off library state and are NOT rewritten by itlkit; if iTunes reconciles them against the .itl it may notice the change

acceptance_criteria: no modal dialog appears in any of the three sessions (iTunesCustomModalDialog window count is 0) and the main window becomes ready in each
no file matching *Damaged* is created in the library directory at any point
iTunes rewrites iTunes Library.itl on quit in each session and itlkit can re-read every capture
after restart 2, itlkit reads exactly one track whose persistent ID is the donor's track persistent ID
that track still carries the donor's name
that track is a member of the master playlist in the restart-2 capture
the COM interface reports a track count of 1 in each session
falsifiers: the track is absent after any restart
iTunes replaces the library with a fresh empty one
outcomes_that_are_not_success: a successful COM AddFile call: this experiment performs no AddFile and no COM mutation of any kind
iTunes generating an empty library: that is a failure, not a pass
the candidate merely being structurally valid to itlkit: itlkit reading its own output proves nothing about native acceptance
the process exiting with code 0: acceptance is judged from the captures and the window state, not from exit codes
uninformative_conditions: if the candidate's bytes are identical to the donor's bytes, the experiment only re-imports what iTunes already wrote; it must be recorded as UNINFORMATIVE and must not be counted as an acceptance result
if delete_track or add_track_from refuses, the result is a REFUSAL record: reportable, and useful, but not an acceptance claim
protocol: 1. this declaration is committed and pushed before the candidate file exists
3. record the candidate's size and digest, and whether it differs from the donor
4. install the candidate as the library and abort if iTunes is already running
5. session 1: launch, wait for the main window, save, quit, capture
8. re-read all three captures with itlkit and evaluate every acceptance criterion mechanically
9. publish the declaration, the outcome, the sanitised session logs and the capture digests

donor.name: iTunes Library.itl
donor.provenance: written by iTunes 12.13.11.1 on quit at the end of the EXP-05B restart-2 session; it is the current live library

what_this_will_not_show: it will not show that a genuinely new track can be constructed: restoration requires a donor from the same library lineage, and three separate refusals block anything else
it will not show that the restored track plays
it will not widen the set of iTunes builds itlkit accepts
it will not generalise past a single-track WAV library on one Windows build
